title: Appendix A — Proposal
text:
Instagram Habits
By Astou, Kalia, & Cassey
Description: We want to research how daily social media usage (hours per day spent scrolling across platforms like Instagram) correlates with self reported stress, anxiety, and mental health across different age groups. We plan to examine public survey databases to analyze these usage patterns and identify trends between time spent online and how it affects one’s mental health.
Questions: - How does daily social media usage correlate with self reported stress or anxiety? - Is there a specific threshold of daily Screen Time where reported stress levels increase significantly? - Do younger demographics of people report higher stress and anxiety levels compared to older age groups when using social media?
Reason/Inspiration: We wanted to see how social media affects daily life and overall well-being. Because social media platforms like Instagram are used by the majority of young adults, they play a massive role in everyday habits. Thus, we are interested in exploring how different levels of screen time impact different people’s mental health. By analyzing public survey data, we want to learn how social media habits are associated with mental disparities and understand whether digital habits are helping or hurting users across different age groups.
Communication Plan: We use Instagram and IMessage to communicate (groupchats).
Roles: Point of Contact: Astou Technical Lead: Kalia Style Lead: Cassey
Conflict Resolution: We’ll talk together in our groupchat, try to find a solution, and ask the professor for guidance. Overall, we will remind each other of deadlines and help each other as needed. If it begins to become uneven, then we can talk to each other (and potentially to the professor).
